title: Retrying Failed Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of retrying failed operations in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply retrying failed operations in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to backoff, timeouts, and idempotency and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Retrying Failed Operations through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding retrying failed operations helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Retrying Failed Operations helps you reason about the retry keyword. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: The retry keyword. Then connect it to Bounded retries. The remaining syllabus points—Backoff, timeouts, and idempotency—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Retrying Failed Operations
content_blocks.code:
attempts = 0
begin
  attempts += 1
  raise "temporary" if attempts < 2
  puts "done after #{attempts} attempt(s)"
rescue RuntimeError
  retry if attempts < 2
end

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports retrying failed operations. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for retrying failed operations using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Backoff, timeouts, and idempotency), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap

Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
